---
title: "Author suggestions"
description: "Credits the authors of new commits, from a pull request or a push, in DESCRIPTION."
aliases:

---

`authors-suggest.yml` looks at every new commit and checks whether its
author is credited in `DESCRIPTION`:
- **on a pull request:** all of the PR's commits when it is opened, then
  each further push's commits;
- **on a push,** if your caller adds that trigger: that push's commits.

What's missing is proposed as a [suggestion PR](suggestions.qmd) into your
branch, titled "Update contributors in DESCRIPTION". Commits merged in from
another branch (e.g. `dev`) and the bot's own commits don't count, see
[what gets reviewed](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-reviewed).

## Roles

- **`aut`** for anyone whose commits changed a file under `R/`;
- **`ctb`** for everyone else — tests, documentation, CI, …
- Someone already listed as `ctb` who now changes `R/` is **upgraded** to
  `aut`. Nobody is ever downgraded or removed, and other roles (`cre`,
  `cph`, …) are left alone.

Merge commits don't count. The suggestion PR's description gives the
reason for each change, e.g. "added as `aut` (changed `R/ds.rse.R`)".

::: {.callout-important}
Trigger the workflow on **all** pull requests (and pushes, if you add
them), without a `paths` filter. Otherwise contributors who only touch
tests or docs are never seen. Schedules and manual runs do nothing: there
is no sweep for authors.
:::

## Names

Authors are resolved to the **name on their GitHub profile**, not the name
in their local git configuration, so a GitHub handle doesn't end up next to
an existing "Real Name" entry. Commits without a linked GitHub account use
the git author name. Bots such as `dependabot[bot]` or
`github-actions[bot]` are skipped; the list lives in
`config/bot-authors.json` and can be [overridden](suggestions.qmd#adjusting-the-guidance).

**Existing entries are recognised** by a commit e-mail that matches the
entry's (GitHub's noreply addresses are ignored), or by the name — ignoring
case, accents, punctuation and word order. E-mails are only used for this
matching and never written to `DESCRIPTION`. If only the family name and
the first initial match ("F. Schwarz" vs. "Florian Schwarz"), nobody is
added; the suggestion PR (or, if nothing else changes, a comment on your
PR) says the person **may already be listed**, so you can decide.

**New people** are added with the name split into given and family name:
the last word is the family name, together with particles such as `van`,
`von` or `de` before it ("Ludwig van Beethoven" → "Ludwig" / "van
Beethoven"). This can't know every naming convention — two-part Spanish
surnames, for example, end up partly in the given name — and a one-word
profile name is flagged in the PR. Check the names before merging.

::: {.callout-note}
`DESCRIPTION` is written with the [desc](https://desc.r-lib.org) package,
which formats `Authors@R` in its standard (tidyverse) layout. A
hand-formatted field is reformatted once, on the first change.
:::
